ai.description: This gecko reaches 18 cm. It is pale grey with faint dorsal bands and a distinctive bright yellow belly. It features large, lidless eyes and expanded, undivided subdigital toe pads.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *H. flaviviridis* by its lack of enlarged, overlapping scales on the underside of the tail, which instead features a single longitudinal row of wide subcaudal plates.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus flaviviridis* is primarily synanthropic, inhabiting human dwellings and stone structures across arid to semi-arid regions, ranging from plains up to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Hemidactylus flaviviridis* is primarily nocturnal, often seen hunting insects near artificial lights where it uses its sticky toe pads to ambush prey on vertical surfaces.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus flaviviridis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs primarily from March to September in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus flaviviridis* is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from arid plains to elevations of 2,000 meters in the Himalayas.
